title: What is RAG?
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with a language model. The system retrieves relevant passages from a knowledge source and supplies them to the model as context before generating an answer.

title: What is a document loader?
content: A document loader imports data from sources such as PDF files, text files, Markdown, HTML pages, Word documents, or databases and converts it into a common document representation for downstream processing.
keywords: document loader, PDF, TXT, Markdown, ingestion

title: What is a Document object?
content: A Document object commonly contains page content and metadata. The page content stores the text, while metadata may include a source filename, page number, URL, author, or other useful attributes.

title: Why split documents into chunks?
content: Long documents are usually split into smaller chunks before embedding and indexing. Chunking helps retrieval return focused passages that fit within model context limits. Chunk size and overlap should be tested for the dataset and use case.
keywords: chunking, chunk size, overlap, context window

title: What is an embedding?
content: An embedding is a numerical vector representing semantic features of text. Embeddings allow a retrieval system to compare a query with document chunks using a similarity measure.

title: What is a vector store?
content: A vector store keeps embedding vectors and associated text or metadata so that a system can retrieve relevant items. Examples of vector databases and indexes include FAISS, Chroma, and managed vector services.

title: How does retrieval work?
content: At query time, the system converts the user's question into a representation compatible with the index, searches for similar chunks, and returns the most relevant results. Retrieval quality depends on chunking, embeddings, metadata, and search configuration.
keywords: query, similarity search, top-k, metadata filtering

title: What does a retriever do?
content: A retriever is an interface or component that accepts a query and returns relevant documents or chunks. It often wraps a vector search, keyword search, hybrid search, or another retrieval strategy.

title: What is the generation step?
content: After retrieval, the application places selected passages into a prompt with the user's question. The language model uses this supplied context to produce an answer. A well-designed system should avoid unsupported claims when the context lacks the answer.
keywords: prompt, context, language model, grounded answer

title: How can RAG answers be evaluated?
content: Evaluate retrieval relevance, answer correctness, faithfulness to retrieved context, source attribution, latency, and cost. Test with representative questions, including questions whose answers are absent from the knowledge base.

title: Common document-loader issues
content: Common loading problems include unsupported file formats, encoding errors, scanned PDFs without OCR, missing permissions, malformed HTML, and empty extracted text. Validate loaded documents before chunking and embedding them.

title: CSV loading tips
content: When loading CSV files, check the delimiter, text encoding, header row, quoting rules, and missing values. Decide whether each row should become a separate document or whether related rows should be grouped together. Preserve useful columns as metadata.
